members.working:
Identify product containing named element for each reaction and determine its geometry.
(i) P₄ + limited Cl₂ → PCl₃ (phosphorus trichloride). PCl₃ has trigonal pyramidal geometry (three Cl atoms and lone pair on P).
(ii) XeF₆ + H₂O hydrolysis → XeO₃ (xenon trioxide). XeO₃ has trigonal pyramidal geometry around Xe (three O atoms and one lone pair).
(iii) NH₄⁺ + NaOH (warm) → NH₃ (ammonia). NH₃ has trigonal pyramidal geometry (three H atoms and one lone pair on N).
(iv) I₂ + conc. HNO₃ (heat) → HIO₃ (iodic acid). I in HIO₃ is bonded to three O atoms and has one lone pair → trigonal pyramidal.
(v) SiCl₄ + Li[AlH₄] → SiH₄ (silane). SiH₄ is tetrahedral (no lone pair).
(vi) PCl₅ + H₂O (complete hydrolysis) → H₃PO₄ (phosphoric acid). P in H₃PO₄ is tetrahedral (four bonds, no lone pair).
(vii) conc. HNO₃ + conc. H₂SO₄ → mixed acid; N ends up in NO₂⁻ or NO₃⁻; geometry around N is trigonal planar (no lone pair on N in NO₂⁻? Actually NO₂⁻ is bent, NO₃⁻ is trigonal planar). Neither is trigonal pyramidal.
Thus reactions with trigonal pyramidal geometry around the named element: (i), (ii), (iii), (iv). That's 4 reactions.
Answer integer 4.
